Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From ac782f4e3bfcde145b8a7f8af31d9422d94d172a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ido Schimmel <idosch@nvidia.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Dec 2025 16:48:28 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ipv4: Fix reference count leak when using error routes with
 nexthop objects

When a nexthop object is deleted, it is marked as dead and then
fib_table_flush() is called to flush all the routes that are using the
dead nexthop.

The current logic in fib_table_flush() is to only flush error routes
(e.g., blackhole) when it is called as part of network namespace
dismantle (i.e., with flush_all=true). Therefore, error routes are not
flushed when their nexthop object is deleted:

 # ip link add name dummy1 up type dummy
 # ip nexthop add id 1 dev dummy1
 # ip route add 198.51.100.1/32 nhid 1
 # ip route add blackhole 198.51.100.2/32 nhid 1
 # ip nexthop del id 1
 # ip route show
 blackhole 198.51.100.2 nhid 1 dev dummy1

As such, they keep holding a reference on the nexthop object which in
turn holds a reference on the nexthop device, resulting in a reference
count leak:

 # ip link del dev dummy1
 [   70.516258] unregister_netdevice: waiting for dummy1 to become free. Usage count = 2

Fix by flushing error routes when their nexthop is marked as dead.

IPv6 does not suffer from this problem.

Fixes: 493ced1ac47c ("ipv4: Allow routes to use nexthop objects")
Reported-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/d943f806-4da6-4970-ac28-b9373b0e63ac@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp/
Reported-by: syzbot+881d65229ca4f9ae8c84@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Ido Schimmel <idosch@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: David Ahern <dsahern@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251221144829.197694-1-idosch@nvidia.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c b/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
index 59a6f0a9638f..7e2c17fec3fc 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
@@ -2053,10 +2053,11 @@ int fib_table_flush(struct net *net, struct fib_table *tb, bool flush_all)
 				continue;
 			}
 
-			/* Do not flush error routes if network namespace is
-			 * not being dismantled
+			/* When not flushing the entire table, skip error
+			 * routes that are not marked for deletion.
 			 */
-			if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error) {
+			if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error &&
+			    !(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD)) {
 				slen = fa->fa_slen;
 				continue;
 			}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in the file `net/ipv4/fib_trie.c`

- **Function:** `fib_table_flush()`
- **Change:** Modified the condition that decides whether to skip flushing error routes when not dismantling the entire network namespace (`flush_all == false`).  
  - **Before:** Error routes were unconditionally skipped when `flush_all` was `false`.  
  - **After:** Error routes are skipped only if `flush_all` is `false` **and** the `fib_info` associated with the route does **not** have the `RTNH_F_DEAD` flag set.  
  - The new condition:  
    ```c
    if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error &&
        !(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD))
    ```
  - This ensures that error routes whose nexthop has been marked as dead (e.g., after a nexthop object deletion) are flushed even when the overall network namespace is not being torn down.

### Relationships

- The bug was a **reference count leak** caused by error routes (like `blackhole`) that continued to hold a reference to a deleted nexthop object, which in turn held a reference to its device. The leak prevented the device from being freed.
- The fix directly addresses the root cause by ensuring that `fib_table_flush()` treats error routes with a dead nexthop the same as other routes in that context—they are removed during a partial flush (i.e., a nexthop deletion event).
- This change is **self-contained** in one function and does not affect other parts of the routing code. IPv6 was not affected because its nexthop handling already avoided this scenario.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error) {</text>
<text>    slen = fa->fa_slen;</text>
<text>    continue;</text>
Reason:
This condition unconditionally skips flushing error routes when `flush_all` is false, even if the route's `fib_info` has the `RTNH_F_DEAD` flag set (i.e., the nexthop object has been deleted). As a result, error routes (e.g., blackhole) that refer to a dead nexthop are never flushed, keeping a reference count on the nexthop and its device, leading to a leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (!flush_all && fib_props[fa->fa_type].error &&</text>
<text>    !(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD)) {</text>
Reason:
The fix adds a check for `!(fi->fib_flags & RTNH_F_DEAD)` to the existing condition. Now error routes are only skipped when `flush_all` is false **and** the route's nexthop is not dead. Error routes whose nexthop has been marked dead (`RTNH_F_DEAD`) are flushed even during a normal (non‑namespace‑dismantle) flush, correctly releasing the reference to the dead nexthop and its device.
